source.title: Treasury Management Strategy 2026/27 — Appendix 1 (194111), Corporate Finance and Performance Overview and Scrutiny Committee, 27 January 2026

facts.note: Appendix p.24 borrowing strategy table: new long-term borrowing rises 0 → 200 → 400 → 600 → 700 → 800 per year, cumulating to £2.7bn by 29/30. Gross external borrowing rises 1,374.7 → 2,218.6 (+844m over six years) as CFR climbs and internal borrowing collapses.

source.title: Treasury Management Strategy 2026/27 — Appendix 1 (194111), Corporate Finance and Performance Overview and Scrutiny Committee, 27 January 2026

facts.note: Appendix p.24. Short-term book stays £625m-£735m across the six-year plan — Cornwall does not shrink short-term borrowing, it stacks new long-term on top of it. Short-term band sits close to the 45% variable-rate upper limit (p.21) and to the 65% under-12-months maturity cap.

source.title: Treasury Management Strategy 2026/27 — Appendix 1 (194111), Corporate Finance and Performance Overview and Scrutiny Committee, 27 January 2026

facts.note: Appendix p.21 footnote 1: 0-65% under-12-months limit 'is set to cover both short-term (temporary borrowing) and the next call date for Lender Option Borrower Options (LOBOs)'. No principal, count, or next-call date disclosed anywhere in the paper. Absence, not zero.

source.title: Canonical break-cost engine (monitor/outreach/canon_break_cost.py) against DMO notice 314/26 PM 2026-08-14

facts.note: 11 of 11 live loans priced. Balance £894.185m, indicative settlement £682.4m. Six long loans (>25y) weighted 2.35% carry the discount; four sub-year loans (weighted 4.85%) sit just above par. Indicative only — the DMO's quote is the only binding one. summary.text:
A candid, CFR-driven strategy — read against a version we already have scored. This paper is the January O&S DRAFT of the 2026/27 TMSS; the final version (s194666) went to Cabinet on 11 February and Full Council on 24 February 2026, and it is that final version the risk profile is anchored to. The Q3 data update shifted CFR 25/26 forecast from £1,736.775m to £1,748.9m, external borrowing 25/26 from £1,536.7m to £1,548.8m, and short-term 25/26 from £661.248m to £673.3m — about £12m added consistently across three balance-sheet lines. Everything qualitative — MRP method, prudential limits, MUFG's rate forecast, counterparty policy, LOBO footnote — is identical between the two.

The liability benchmark stance is unusually candid. Appendix p.8: 'The graph shows that the Council is over the benchmark' and 'Being over the Liability Benchmark is a conscious decision, as the Council's current strategy is to use the most efficient mix of borrowing and investment, to produce the lowest net interest cost to the Council and the taxpayer.' Most councils that sit over their benchmark do not say so this plainly. The reasoning aligns with MUFG's own advice printed inside the paper (p.23): 'As all PWLB certainty rates are currently significantly above [neutral], borrowing strategies will need to be reviewed in that context. Overall, better value can currently be obtained from shorter-dated borrowing.'

The scale is the story. Gross external borrowing rises from £1,374.7m (31/3/25 actual) to £2,218.6m (31/3/30) — a £843.9m increase over six years, on top of a CFR climbing £1,568m to £2,292m over the same window. Internal borrowing collapses from £100m to £15m from 26/27 onward, and the strategy stacks a cumulative £2.7bn of new long-term borrowing on top of a short-term book that stays £625m–£735m throughout. Cash investments run from £354m to a £100m floor from 28/29, driven by the Dedicated Schools Grant deficit being physically spent down — the paper is explicit that the cash rundown is the DSG balance-sheet effect, not treasury management. The GF financing-cost ratio rises 5.8% → 8.4% against a 9% limit cut from 11% in the previous cycle; the HRA ratio reaches 14.6% with borrowing per HRA dwelling rising £18,029 → £25,578.

Our PWLB file holds 11 live loans totalling £894.185m at a weighted 3.6375%. The paper publishes no loan-book table, so we cannot tie to a printed figure — but the residual ~£642m between our PWLB total and the paper's £1,536.7m external is consistent with heavy LA-to-LA short-term borrowing, which p.19 explicitly names as Cornwall's first-choice short-term source. Six long loans (over 25 years, weighted 2.35%) sit well below par: the canonical engine prices the 11-loan book at about £682.4m against £894.2m balance — an indicative discount near £212m. Indicative only, no MRP or accounting treatment modelled, DMO the only binding quote. LOBOs are held but the paper never quantifies them (p.21 footnote acknowledges their existence within the under-12-months maturity limit).

Borrowing-strategy table on p.24 rebuilds the aggregate on p.18 to the pound. Loan-count/weighted-rate reconciliation to the paper is NOT POSSIBLE — Cornwall publishes no loan-book table in this TMSS. || The paper is the January O&S DRAFT, not the version Full Council approved on 24 February 2026 (s194666). Balance-sheet lines moved ~£12m consistently on the Q3 data update; qualitative content identical. officer.reason: Source paper (s194110/s194111) is the January O&S draft. Full Council approved a revised version (s194666) on 24 February 2026 in which the current-year balance-sheet lines (CFR 25/26, external 25/26, short-term 25/26) each moved ~£12m. Drafting the officer email off this document would quote out-of-date figures to a treasurer whose team refers to the final version. The risk profile at monitor/risk/profiles/E06000052.json is anchored to s194666 and holds the current numbers; a future draft should be built from there.
officer.notes_to_next_drafter: Hooks available in the final paper that don't need re-verification: (1) the 'conscious decision' quote on the liability benchmark position — unusually candid and identical between versions; (2) MUFG's own advice printed inside the paper — 'better value can currently be obtained from shorter-dated borrowing' — as the explicit reason for the short-first strategy Cornwall is running; (3) the shape of the six-year plan — £2.7bn cumulative new long-term borrowing stacked on top of a £625m–£735m short-term book that never shrinks, and internal borrowing collapsing from £100m to £15m; (4) the DSG cash-rundown from £354m to a £100m floor from 28/29 — explicitly attributed to the deficit being physically spent, not to treasury choices. The paper does not publish a PWLB loan-book table, so open with the qualitative hook not with the loan-book reconciliation. The S151 is not named in either paper — verify title from s194666 before addressing. Authors Katey Durkin (Service Director for Resources and Performance, katey.durkin@cornwall.gov.uk) and Sean Johns (Head of Pensions and Treasury, sean.johns@cornwall.gov.uk) are named on this draft.
